question_text: A bag contains 3 red tickets and 2 blue tickets. Tickets are selected from the bag, without replacement, until at least one ticket of each colour is selected. Let $X$ be the total number of tickets selected.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Identify the number of draws required until a condition is met (sampling without replacement).
step_by_step: Minimum draws is 2 (e.g., BR or RB).
Maximum draws occurs if same colors are picked first, stopping when one of each is obtained, giving at most 4 draws.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including 1, which is impossible since at least two tickets are needed to have tickets of both colors.

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculate probabilities for each outcome using conditional probability without replacement

subparts.solution:
Let B represent a blue ticket, and R represent a red ticket.
The possible selections that can be made are:
$\begin{aligned} &\text{BR} \quad (X = 2) \\ &\text{RB} \\ &\text{BBR} \quad (X = 3) \\ &\text{RRB} \\ &\text{RRRB} \quad (X = 4) \end{aligned}$

So,
$\begin{aligned} P(X = 2) &= \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{3}{4} + \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} = \frac{3}{5} \\ P(X = 3) &= \frac{2}{5} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{3} + \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} \times \frac{2}{3} = \frac{3}{10} \\ P(X = 4) &= \frac{3}{5} \times \frac{2}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{2}{2} = \frac{1}{10} \end{aligned}$

$\therefore$ the probability distribution of $X$ is:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|} \hline x & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ \hline P(X = x) & \frac{3}{5} & \frac{3}{10} & \frac{1}{10} \\ \hline \end{array}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Calculate probability of sequences of selections without replacement and construct the probability distribution table.
step_by_step: For $X=2$: outcomes are BR and RB. $P(BR) = \frac{2}{5}\times\frac{3}{4} = \frac{3}{10}$, $P(RB) = \frac{3}{5}\times\frac{2}{4} = \frac{3}{10}$. Total = $\frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}$.
For $X=3$: outcomes are BBR and RRB. $P(BBR) = \frac{2}{5}\times\frac{1}{4}\times 1 = \frac{1}{10}$, $P(RRB) = \frac{3}{5}\times\frac{2}{4}\times\frac{2}{3} = \frac{2}{10}$. Total = $\frac{3}{10}$.
Present as a distribution table and check sum equals 1.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to reduce the total number of tickets in the denominator after each draw (sampling without replacement).

subparts.solution: It is most likely that 2 tickets are drawn, so the mode is 2.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The mode is the value of $x$ that corresponds to the largest probability $P(X=x)$.
step_by_step: Since $0.6$ is the highest probability, the mode is 2.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Writing the probability $\frac{3}{5}$ instead of the value $2$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Expected value is the sum of products of each outcome and its probability: $E(X) = \sum x P(X=x)$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Dividing by the number of outcomes instead of computing the weighted sum.
